3 · How the model treats them

A station passes flow only through open valves

Station 12 showed the hardware. The simulator turns it into one opening.

$v$
control-valve opening set by its controller
%
$V$
effective opening of the whole station
%
$b_1, b_2, y$
upstream block, downstream block, by-pass: 1 open, 0 closed
–
$B$
full by-pass as control-valve opening (HV_BYP, assumed)
40 %
$V = b_1\,b_2\,v + y\,B$both blocks needed; by-pass adds in parallel
$V \leftarrow \min(100,\ \max(0,\ V))$a station cannot exceed fully open

Pumps: runs only with suction AND discharge open.

Interactive · model runs, valve moved at 30 s, trips active

One hand valve can stop the unit

Closing the running pump's suction trips R-101 in under three minutes; the spare's suction changes nothing until the spare is needed.

Interactive · open MV-308 around FV-101

FIC-101 closes FV-101 by what the by-pass passes

Station$V = b_1 b_2\,v + y\,B$

The flow holds at 34.8 t/h while $v = V - B \ge 0$; past that the controller has lost its handle.

5 · What you may not move

The tab refuses six valves, with the reason

Close-up of an operable valve: Open / Close

  • LO MV-309, MV-414: car seal, permit and key.
  • Drains MV-305, MV-310, MV-321, MV-405: isolated, drained line under permit.
  • Standby F-102: follows the Field tab selector.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • 43 of 49 hand valves are operable; six are refused.
  • A station passes $b_1 b_2 v + yB$.
  • A closed running-pump valve trips the unit; a spare's does not.
  • An open by-pass steals the controller's range.

Part 3 · The rounds sheet

How is a round written down and checked against the plant?

Part 3 · the plan

A round is a written record

  1. The rounds sheet28 rows, station by station
  2. Reading tolerancewhen an entry counts as right
  3. The event logwhat each field action writes
  4. Identificationblank boxes, 90 % target

Interactive · pick a station

28 rows: readings, positions, running pumps

Each row is checked against the plant at the moment of checking, not against the design.

Interactive · enter a reading

An entry counts when it is within the tolerance

Every number row of the sheet is judged by one rule.

$$|a - x| \le \delta$$

$a$ entry · $x$ plant now · $\delta$ tolerance (flows $0.03\,x$)

Plant values: design state of the model. Read to the tolerance, not to the last digit.

Interactive · step through one visit to station 12

Every field action leaves a line in the log

The Debrief tab reads these lines: an unread gauge leaves no trace. Values: design state.

4 · Identification

Blank boxes: name every valve and gauge

Identify mode: numbered boxes, no tags

$$p = 100\,\frac{n_{ok}}{n} \ \ge\ 90\ \%$$

$n_{ok}$ correct boxes, $n$ boxes over all stations.

  • Tag sprites hide: no give-away.
  • Check each station, then the total.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The sheet has 28 rows over the stations.
  • An entry counts within $\pm\delta$ of the plant now.
  • Reads, checks and valve moves are logged.
  • Identification passes at 90 %.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the fourteen stations in order; know each gauge's level.

2

Check hand-valve positions in the field: the board cannot see them.

3

Never close a running pump's suction or discharge.

4

Leave car-sealed valves and drains alone without a permit.

5

Write every reading down within its tolerance; the log keeps the rest.
